description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §6.6.5 'Build-time evaluation scope': every reference resolved BEFORE the simulation runs — a coordinate-expression `ic` (§11.4.1) and an inline analytic assertion `reference` — binds the model's parameters to their `parameter_overrides`-or-default values, with the overrides keyed by LOCAL parameter name (§6.6). Parameter `A` (default 1.0) appears ONLY inside `ic(u)` and inside assertion references, never in an equation, so a test that overrides `A` can change the answer through the build-time scope and nowhere else. State `v` is seeded by the parameter-FREE `ic(v) = cos(pi x)` and is the independent anchor the parameter-dependent `reference` is measured against, so a binding that ignored the override in BOTH the ic and the reference cannot have the two errors cancel and still pass. Julia's tree-walk build previously resolved `parameter_overrides` by EXACT key against the flattening-qualified parameter name (`M.A`), so the spec-spelled local key (`A`) missed: the run silently used the default and the inline test still reported a verdict. Python (`_resolve_override`: exact key, then bare trailing segment) and Rust (`normalize_override_keys`: strip the single-model `<namespace>.` prefix) already honoured the local spelling. Julia is the reference binding: its `run_pde_tests` minted golden/ic_param_override.json.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator / inline PDE-test runner
